expectations.text: An MP4 deliverable exists, larger than 100 KB
The MP4 video stream is H.264 with yuv420p pixel format (ffprobe codec_name=h264, pix_fmt=yuv420p)
The MP4 has even width and height (yuv420p requirement satisfied in the file itself)
The MP4 duration is between 6 and 12 seconds (user asked ~8s; frame-driven duration must be lengthened via playback speed)
The video actually animates: a frame extracted at 25% of the timeline differs from one at 75%
A PNG deliverable exists at 2000+ pixels on its long side showing the peptide cartoon

notes: Notable workaround: the old export.py's `--seconds 8` initially produced a 4.66 s video because the browser recorder auto-stops after one 40-frame pass, beating the timer — the runner had to hand-inject a script into viewer.html setting renderer.animationSpeed=185 and re-export with `--seconds 12` to land at 8.2 s. It also authored spec_movie.json/spec_still.json declaratively (old skill's only styling route) and self-verified with ffprobe, ffmpeg freezedetect, and extracted-frame comparison. 6/6, but only via HTML surgery that the new skill's --speed flag makes unnecessary.
